newsitem.title: UK: UK minister urges firms to act on modified maize.
newsitem.headline: UK minister urges firms to act on modified maize.

text.p: The government urged British food manufacturers and retailers on Thursday to provide information for consumers about the use of genetically modified maize (GMM).
The European Union in December cleared imports of GMM into Europe, overriding British qualms about whether it could be used safely in unprocessed form in animal feeds.
Appearing at question time in parliament, junior agriculture minister Angela Browning was urged to persuade the European Commission to reimpose a ban on unprocessed GMM.
MPs also called for GMM to be segregated from non-modified maize to permit clear labelling and allay public anxiety.
Browning said it was not in her power to ban the new product because Britain's arguments had been rejected by the EU in an area that was subject to qualified majority voting.

"If I were to insist that only segregated crops came into this country, first of all I would be in contravention of the European Union rules and on a worldwide basis I would be contravention of World Trade Organisation rules," she said.

However, it was quite possible for companies to state publicly whether or not they would buy modified foods. "It is a matter for the industry, whom we're very supportive of, to source their product... by making it very clear what they will and what they won't buy," she said.
Browning said she had already held meetings with the food manufacturing industry.

She was speaking hours after Tesco, one of Britain's leading food retailers, said it would label genetically modified foods, thereby requiring suppliers to segregate ingredients into modified and unmodified groups.
